Subject: POC Acceptance Gates, Tech Leads & Procurement Path

Thanks again for taking the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the pilot timeline. High-level items we agreed on during the demo: bullets below are my read of the acceptance criteria and owners; please correct where I'm wrong.

Acceptance gates (candidate KPIs):
- End-to-end latency under 150ms p95 for single-query flows (90% of calls)
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled sample set
- Throughput of 250 req/s sustained during simulated peak windows
- No plaintext customer PII persisted in logs (security check)

Proposed owners (please confirm):
- Infra / provisioning: Tom Wilson (Skyline)
- App integration / API surface: Alice Nguyen (Skyline)
- Security / compliance signoff: Raj Patel (Skyline)
- Procurement / legal: Linda Gomez (Skyline)
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter
- Redwood SE: Priyom Das
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Emily to confirm acceptance gates and internal owners (by EOD 7/13) — we need a clear SCM to run the load tests.
2) Redwood to send a short SOW + evaluation plan and an infra checklist (by 7/13).
3) Goal: POC kickoff week of 7/19 with a 4-week evaluation window.

Attachments: I'll attach a 1-page SOW draft and a sample eval criteria spreadsheet for you to annotate.

If the owner mapping above is off, please reply inline so I can update the RACI.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: POC Acceptance Gates, Tech Leads & Procurement Path

Thanks Ben — appreciate the concise recap. Confirming owners and a couple clarifications: we can commit to the proposed owners but want to make the acceptance gates slightly more specific for tooling purposes.

Clarified acceptance criteria:
- Latency: 95th percentile under 150ms for the web callback path; background batch scoring can be higher (documented).
- Accuracy: >= 92% intent classification on the 1,200-label holdout set we'll share; we expect Redwood to run initial baseline tests against our set.
- Throughput: 250 req/s sustained for 30 minutes with a 2x spike test to 500 req/s for 5 minutes.
- Security: no plaintext PII in logs; also require TLS mutual-auth between our API gateway and Redwood for the trial.

Owners confirmed:
- Infra: Tom Wilson (tom.wilson@skyline-retail.com)
- App: Alice Nguyen (alice.nguyen@skyline-retail.com)
- Security: Raj Patel (raj.patel@skyline-retail.com)
- Procurement: Linda Gomez (linda.gomez@skyline-retail.com)

Procurement note: Linda says typical procurement paperwork will take ~2–3 weeks after SOW is accepted; she can fast-track for proof-of-value purchases if we keep the SOW minimal.

Emily
VP Product | Skyline Retail
emily.hart@skyline-retail.com

All — I can take point on the Redwood side for technical onboarding. Two quick items and a poll for kickoff times: 

1) Infra checklist summary (high level):
- Network: allow egress to runtime.redwood.inference.com, open outbound port 443, confirm TLS mutual-auth cert exchange method.
- Data: provide sanitized sample dataset (S3 link) and schema; we will only use a subset for accuracy tests.
- Access: create a scoped service account for Redwood with permissions to post events to your staging API endpoint.
- Load testing: confirm whether Skyline wants Redwood to run the load generator from our dedicated test pool (recommended) or run internally (provide bastion/egress IPs).

2) Kickoff poll (pick one):
- Option A: Monday 7/19 10:00am PT (preferred for Redwood SE availability)
- Option B: Monday 7/19 2:00pm PT

If you confirm owners and pick a kickoff time, we'll lock the SOW and get procurement moving. I've attached a minimal SOW and the evaluation spreadsheet; Linda — if you can confirm procurement path that helps shorten the loop.

Thanks,
